diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says GND, datasheet reading says Terminal 1
diffs.evidence: Same physical tab, different name. Paradise Arcade's OBSF-30 page: ".110\" quick connects ... Switch(SW-68) ... Rating: DC12V100mA Insulation resistance (IR): DC250V/50MΩ over between terminals". The SW-68 is a two-terminal normally-open switch, and the vendors give the tabs no labels and no polarity. 'Terminal 1' is just a generic name. The part names the same unmarked tab by its job in the recommended wiring (to ground, with the other tab pulled up to a GPIO). Its description says the switch is 'not polarised', so either tab can be GND. The wiring and electrical meaning do not change.

diffs.diff: header pin 2: part says SIG, datasheet reading says Terminal 2
diffs.evidence: Same physical tab, different name. Focus Attack's SW-68 page (filed under 'Microswitches .110\" Terminal') lists 'Rating: DC12V100mA ... Withstanding voltage: terminals between AC250V/1 minutes'. That is one contact between two unmarked, interchangeable terminals. 'Terminal 2' is the generic name; the part calls the second tab SIG because it goes to the GPIO with the internal pull-up (reads 0 when pressed). Swapping the two tabs gives identical behaviour, so the model's pin names are correct.
